key_facts: A well-demarcated erosion, ulcer or shiny membrane on the vertex scalp at birth, healing to a hairless scar.
Varied causes: genetic, teratogens (carbimazole or methimazole), intrauterine infection, vascular disruption, amniotic bands.
Small and superficial: gentle cleansing, bland ointment and protection from trauma.
Hair collar sign (possible neural tube defect), a large midline defect (sagittal sinus), and ACC with blistering (EB) or limb defects (Adams–Oliver).

sections.title: Overview
blocks: Congenital **focal absence of skin**. Depth varies from epidermis only through to bone or dura. Most often it is a **solitary scalp vertex** defect. It may be isolated or part of a syndrome (e.g. **Adams–Oliver**, or **Bart syndrome** when limb ACC occurs with EB).

ul: Genetic factors (e.g. BMS1 and other loci).
Intrauterine infection (varicella, HSV), vascular disruption, amniotic bands, fetus papyraceus.
Tension at the hair whorl during rapid fetal brain growth.
Well-demarcated **ulcer, erosion, membrane or bullous lesion** on the vertex scalp at birth, healing to an **alopecic scar**.
Less often on the trunk or limbs.
**Hair collar sign:** a ring of darker, longer, coarser hair around a scalp lesion. It marks possible **cranial dysraphism or ectopic neural tissue** (encephalocele or meningocele spectrum).
Large midline defects, vascular stains or neurological signs increase the risk of underlying skull or CNS involvement.

sections.title: Diagnosis and investigations
blocks: Clinical at birth. Document size and depth. **Imaging** (ultrasound ± MRI) for large, midline, deep or hair-collar lesions. Exclude birth-trauma mimics (forceps, scalp electrode) from the history and appearance. Genetic or syndrome work-up if there are other anomalies.

sections.title: Differential diagnoses
blocks: Birth trauma, herpes erosions, EB with congenital absence of skin, sebaceous naevus, heterotopic brain tissue, and sinus pericranii.

ul: **Small, superficial lesions:** usually heal with conservative care. Cleanse gently, apply a bland ointment (± a topical antibacterial if infected), and protect from trauma.

**Large, deep, multiple, hair-collar or midline lesions:** urgent paediatric, plastic surgery or neurosurgery input. Grafting or careful dressings may be needed to prevent **sagittal sinus haemorrhage** and infection.
**Counselling:** a scar and bald patch may remain. The teratogen history matters for future pregnancy counselling (specialist or obstetric).
**Pharmacist angle:** know the carbimazole/methimazole association. **Do not stop** maternal antithyroid treatment without obstetric or endocrine advice; flag the association to specialists.

pearls: Ask about maternal medicines in pregnancy, especially antithyroid drugs.
Most small defects heal well, so reassure while arranging appropriate follow-up.
